title: CastillosCVEP100
description: A code-VEP brain-computer interface dataset from 12 healthy participants comparing burst c-VEP and m-sequence stimulation paradigms at two amplitude depths (100% and 40%). The study evaluates classification performance and user experience using 32-channel EEG recorded at 500 Hz. The dataset includes 2 classification classes with 4 experimental conditions (burst/m-sequence × 100%/40% amplitude). CNN-based decoding achieves up to 95.6% accuracy with full calibration data (52.8s), with typical performance around 85% accuracy. This derivative dataset optimizes stimulus design for reactive BCI applications while maintaining visual comfort.
methods_description: EEG data acquired from 12 healthy participants using a BrainProducts LiveAmp 32-channel system at 500 Hz sampling rate with standard 10-20 montage (reference: FCz, ground: FPz). Participants performed a 4-class visual attention task with four cued targets presented sequentially for 0.5 s, followed by 2.2 s stimulation phase. Four experimental conditions tested: burst c-VEP and m-sequence c-VEP, each at 100% and 40% amplitude depth. Data processed with CNN-based classification using 250 ms sliding windows with 2 ms stride and standard deviation normalization. Subjective ratings collected for visual comfort, mental tiredness, and intrusiveness.
